# bifrost_model_limit (Resource)

Manages a Bifrost model limit (model config): standalone budgets and a rate limit applied to a model, optionally narrowed to a provider, globally or within a scope.

~> **Virtual-key scope:** Bifrost stores a virtual key's own `budgets` as a `virtual_key`-scoped model limit with `model_name = "*"`, so do not declare that combination here. Per-model limits scoped to a virtual key are deleted by Bifrost when the key no longer lists their provider in `provider_configs`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Global spend cap and rate limit for gpt-4o on OpenAI, independent of any virtual key.
resource "bifrost_model_limit" "gpt4o" {
  model_name    = "gpt-4o"
  provider_name = "openai"

  budgets = [
    {
      max_limit      = 500
      reset_duration = "1M"
    },
    {
      max_limit      = 50
      reset_duration = "1d"
    },
  ]

  rate_limit = {
    request_max_limit      = 1000
    request_reset_duration = "1m"
  }
}

# Per-model budget within a single virtual key. The key must list the provider in provider_configs.
resource "bifrost_model_limit" "team_gpt4o" {
  model_name    = "gpt-4o"
  provider_name = "openai"
  scope         = "virtual_key"
  scope_id      = bifrost_virtual_key.team_key.id

  budgets = [
    {
      max_limit      = 25
      reset_duration = "1w"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `model_name` (String) Model the limit applies to. Use `*` to match all models.

### Optional

- `budgets` (Attributes List) Budget configurations. Each entry must have a unique `reset_duration` (e.g. `1d`, `1w`, `1M`). Resets are calendar-aligned only for `virtual_key` scope when the owning key sets `calendar_aligned`. Sending an empty list clears all existing budgets on update. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--budgets))
- `provider_name` (String) Provider name (e.g. `openai`). Omit to apply to the model on every provider. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `rate_limit` (Attributes) Rate-limit configuration. Reset durations accept Bifrost duration strings such as `1m` or `1h`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit))
- `scope` (String) Where the limit applies: `global`, `virtual_key`, or `project` (_enterprise_). Defaults to `global`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `scope_id` (String) ID of the scope target (virtual key or project ID). Required when `scope` is not `global`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID assigned by Bifrost at creation time.

<a id="nestedatt--budgets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `budgets`

Required:

- `max_limit` (Number) Maximum budget in dollars.
- `reset_duration` (String) Budget reset period (e.g. `1d`, `1w`, `1M`). Must be unique within the list.


<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit`

Optional:

- `request_max_limit` (Number) Maximum request count per window.
- `request_reset_duration` (String) Request-limit reset window (e.g. `1m`, `1h`).
- `token_max_limit` (Number) Maximum token count per window.
- `token_reset_duration` (String) Token-limit reset window (e.g. `1m`, `1h`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Model limits are imported by their UUID (the `id` returned at creation time).
terraform import bifrost_model_limit.gpt4o 3f1c9a2e-...
```
